text:
Blabbering. 

I’m not posting this to get sympathy or anything like that as I’ve previously said I wouldn’t change anything. It’s just a little insight to my younger life which played out like a movie. 

So my dad after he got out of prison for time already served, ten years, which was his second stint for drug smuggling, organized crime. He was supposed to serve life but he flipped and took the feds to where another mobster’s body was buried. At this point he’s old, has COPD from smoking most of his life, weak, broken by a rough choices. A far cry from the indestructible bad ass and trouble maker he was when I was young. Myself, my mom and my siblings were literally terrified of this version of him. Especially when he drank! 

Anyway him and I are driving after he’s been out for a few weeks. I ask him if he’s watched The Sopranos which was big at the time. He says no, what’s it about. I say it’s about the mafia. He says he won’t watch it and wants nothing to do with the mob. That it was the biggest mistake of his fucking  life! I was kinda surprised but totally got it. 

He passed about ten years ago. He had said previously his own father was on a ventilator for weeks before he passed and he didn’t want to go through that. The hospital stuck one in him anyway, against what was written on the chart. My dad didn’t want this. He was semi unconscious. We said dad, if you want the ventilator out raise your right hand which he did. We asked the same question again to verify, same raising of hand. We said dad, you understand if we remove the ventilator you’re going to die. He raised his hand, he was ready to go. I had to leave the room because I broke down. Once removed his breaths became shorter and shorter and after about 7 hours he had passed. A rough patch in my life obviously. I cried for two or three nights. My youngest who was around 5 or so at the time was by my side every night comforting me as I cried. Sad but a beautiful thing! 

At his viewing I saw his younger brother, my uncle. He tells me my dad had told him his greatest regret in life was not spending more time with his son when I was young. Oh that killed me. 

About a month ago it kinda hit me out of nowhere as I thought about my dad and my crazy but amazing childhood that after everything I’d seen concerning him growing up and his behavior and life choices, the way he treated my mom that he was my was still truly my hero. 

The End
